use_case_name: Generate Treatment Quality and Trend Reports

claims.content: To generate analytical, medical, financial, and statistical reports summarizing treatment quality, syndrome frequencies, provider performance, and time trends for monitoring and evaluation purposes.

goal.raw_text: To generate analytical, medical, financial, and statistical reports summarizing treatment quality, syndrome frequencies, provider performance, and time trends for monitoring and evaluation purposes.

claims.content: MSIU Field Office User
The system must have collected and processed claim data from Voucher Service Providers (VSPs), including treatment details, syndrome diagnoses, lab tests, drugs administered, and patient outcomes.
Client feedback data must have been captured via the voucher system for treated clients, including satisfaction levels, referral information, and partner treatment status.
Master data for syndromes, clinical examinations, diagnosis codes, lab tests, drugs, and patient statuses must be populated in the system to enable accurate categorization and reporting.
The MSIU Field Office User must be logged into the system with appropriate user group privileges that allow access to report generation modules.
The system must have stored historical claim and feedback records over multiple periods (monthly, quarterly, half-yearly) to enable trend analysis.
The MSIU Field Office User initiates the report generation process to review treatment quality, syndrome frequencies, provider performance, and time trends for monitoring and evaluation purposes.

trigger.raw_text: The MSIU Field Office User initiates the report generation process to review treatment quality, syndrome frequencies, provider performance, and time trends for monitoring and evaluation purposes.

claims.content: The MSIU Field Office User navigates to the Reports module within the VMUS system.
The user selects the option to generate 'Standard and Customized' reports as defined in section 6 of the SRS.

The system presents available report types including: 'Report, summarising all providers', 'Quarterly summary reports per provider and summarising all providers', 'Frequencies of syndromes treated, additional information on patient population (sex, age)', 'Frequencies of primary clients and notified partners', 'Number of correctly documented cases, cases with incorrect documentation, cases treated according to algorithms, cases with justified treatment alterations and treatment errors', 'Summary report comparing the different providers regarding syndromes treated, documentation quality and treatment behaviour', and 'Quarterly and half yearly reports giving the time trends of the above-mentioned indicators for each provider and all providers combined'.
The user selects one or more specific report types based on monitoring needs (e.g., trend analysis, provider comparison, syndrome frequency).
If applicable, the user specifies parameters such as date range (monthly, quarterly, half-yearly), provider(s) to include, syndrome type, or geographic region.
The system retrieves relevant data from the database, including claim records, client feedback, master data (syndromes, drugs, diagnoses), and historical trends.

The system processes the data according to the selected report logic — aggregating counts, calculating frequencies, comparing providers, identifying documentation errors, and computing time-based trends.
The system generates the report output in a readable format (e.g., tabular, graphical, or printed layout) displaying analytical, medical, financial, and statistical summaries as specified.
The system displays the generated report to the user, allowing options to view, print, export, or save the report.
The user reviews the report for insights into treatment quality, syndrome patterns, provider performance, and temporal trends to support decision-making and program evaluation.

If the user selects a report type that requires specific parameters (e.g., date range, provider, syndrome) but does not provide them, the system prompts the user to enter the missing mandatory parameters before proceeding.

If the system finds no data matching the selected report criteria (e.g., no claims in the specified date range or for the selected provider), it displays a message indicating 'No data available for the selected criteria' and returns to the report selection screen.

If during data processing the system encounters incomplete or inconsistent master data (e.g., missing syndrome code or drug price), it logs a warning and may exclude affected records from the report, notifying the user of potential data quality issues in the report footer or a separate alert.

If the user requests a customized report format not predefined in the system, and the system lacks the capability to generate it dynamically, it informs the user that only standard reports are currently supported and offers to escalate the request to the system administrator or development team.

If the generated report exceeds system display limits (e.g., too many rows or complex graphics), the system offers pagination, export options (PDF/Excel), or suggests filtering criteria to reduce output size.

If the user fails to provide mandatory parameters (such as date range or provider selection) required for a specific report type, the system validates the input and displays an error message prompting for the missing information, preventing report generation until resolved.

If the system queries the database based on the user's selected criteria (e.g., specific time period or provider) and finds no matching claim or feedback records, it displays a 'No data available' notification and returns the user to the report selection interface without generating an empty report.

During the aggregation process for quality reports (e.g., 'cases treated according to algorithms'), if the system encounters claim records with missing mandatory clinical data (diagnosis, drugs) or inconsistent master data, it categorizes these records as 'Incorrect Documentation' or 'Treatment Errors' rather than crashing, ensuring the report reflects data quality issues.

If the user attempting to access the Reports module or specific analytical reports lacks the necessary 'User Group' privileges defined in the Security settings, the system denies access and displays an authorization error.

If the requested report scope (e.g., 'half yearly trends for all providers') exceeds system display or memory limits, the system may fail to render the view and instead offers the user options to export the raw data or reduce the scope of the request.

The system has generated and displayed a report containing analytical, medical, financial, and statistical data regarding treatment quality, syndrome frequencies, provider performance, or time trends as requested by the user.

The specific indicators defined in Section 6 have been calculated and presented: 'Number of correctly documented cases', 'cases with incorrect documentation', 'cases treated according to algorithms', 'cases with justified treatment alterations', and 'treatment errors'.

If a trend report was selected, the system has successfully aggregated historical data to show time trends for each provider and all providers combined over monthly, quarterly, or half-yearly periods.
If a provider comparison report was selected, the system has presented a summary comparing different providers regarding syndromes treated, documentation quality, and treatment behavior.
The user has reviewed the output to support monitoring and evaluation of the voucher scheme's operation.
